messages:
oncall-bot: Pager alert — P1: Autoscaler failing to provision GPUs in azure-northcentral. Significant queue growth on inference-prod-eu; multiple customer errors. Paging oncall.
Samir: I'm on it. Acknowledging pager. First pass: check autoscaler and cloud errors.
Jen: Seeing user-facing 429/503s for generation endpoints, queue length up ~2.4k in router. Clients hitting timeouts at 30s. :grimacing:
Mike: Autoscaler logs -> repeated VM create failures. Error: \"Operation could not be completed: QuotaExceeded (Requested cores/GPUs exceed subscription limits)\". Azure API 403 on create.
Alisa: Running az commands now. `az vm list-usage --location northcentralus` shows GPU count at 100% and vCPU soft limits hit. Also `az vm create` attempts get throttled with 429 from compute.
Samir: Which pool is impacted? Is it only inference-prod-eu or others too?
Jen: Primarily the northcentral region pool 'inference-prod-east' used for fallback from apac. We're seeing cross-region routing try to failover here and get queued.
Customer-SRE: We're already getting inbound from a customer support ticket (enterprise account) reporting increased latency and some failed jobs. They have heavy batch traffic right now.
SRE-Lead: Any automatic fallback policies in play? Can we route to another region while we mitigate?
Mike: Smart routing tried to fall back to eu-west but eu-west pools are at ~85% and we refused additional placement to avoid saturation. Fallback cascade exhausted.
Alisa: Quick mitigation options:
- Try manual routing rule to divert non-enterprise traffic to eu-west (if headroom allows)
- Spin up smaller instance types w/out GPUs and fallback to CPU quantized model for low-priority traffic
- Request quota increase from Azure (slow)
Samir: Start customer impact assessment: which customers are affected and what % of traffic? Jen, can you grab recent logs and map to top 10 customers?
Jen: Pulling logs... (snippet) `router.queue_length: 2440, error_rate: 0.28, top_customers: [acme(34%), beta-saas(18%), gamma-ml(10%)]`
Customer-SRE: Acme is on enterprise contract — alert sales and start customer comms. Preparing status note.
SRE-Lead: Who's owning the cloud quota escalation? Mike, Alisa, coordinate with cloud ops and open an expedited support request.
Mike: Opening Azure support SR now. SR#: 2026-00034567. Request: GPU quota increase + vCPU softlimit removal for subscription xxxxx. ETA unknown. Marking as escalated.
Alisa: While support is processing, I'm going to attempt a manual temp mitigation: carve a small assignment from a low-impact pool and shift to it. Will try `az vm create --size Standard_NC6s_v3` in westus2 where we have spare quota.
Samir: Make sure we set autoscaler to ignore the failed zone for now. Patch: `autoscaler.policy.exclude_regions += [\"northcentralus\"]` (dry run first).
Jen: Patch applied to canary route, verifying: canary saw reduced queue from 1200 -> 700 after diversion to westus2. :thumbsup:
Customer-SRE: Sending initial customer note to Acme: short, technical, ETA: investigating and working on failover. Will include mitigation steps and followups.
Mike: Azure SR update: vendor responded — they can expedite but need justification and peak history. Support suggests we provide recent usage CSV; they've put the request in \"billing review\" queue.
SRE-Lead: Meanwhile, temporarily scale down batch jobs for non-critical tenants. Can we pause scheduled retrains or background embeddings jobs?
Alisa: Pausing low-priority batch job pipeline `embeddings-nightly` across tenants `beta-saas`, `gamma-ml` — issuing `kubectl scale job embeddings-nightly --replicas=0` in our control plane.
Jen: repo telemetry shows immediate small drop in queue, but still high due to live traffic.
Samir: Root cause summary so far: Azure GPU quota exhausted in northcentral due to unexpected spike + autoscaler attempted scale-up into the constrained region; autoscaler did not transparently reroute some requests causing queue growth and customer impact.
Customer-SRE: Tracking impacted customer list: acme, beta-saas, gamma-ml, delta-ads. Prioritizing Acme and Delta (enterprise / high-SLA) for manual routing to westus2.
Mike: Created temporary capacity in westus2: 12 NC6s instances booted, added to inference-prod fallback pool. Confirmed they registered with runtime, KV caches primed ~20%.
Jen: After adding westus2, queue decreased to ~420, error rate down to 7%. But we still have throttling on new instance creation in northcentral causing autoscaler to keep failing — need longer-term fix.
SRE-Lead: Next steps:
1) Keep Azure SR open and push for quota increase (Mike)
2) Maintain manual routing to westus2 and monitor costs (Samir)
3) Add autoscaler policy to avoid regions failing on quota errors and prefer multi-region placement (Engineering follow-up ticket) (Alisa)
4) Customer comms and postmortem (Customer-SRE + Jen)
Samir: I'll take the handoff for the next hour. @SRE-Lead, please escalate any exec stakeholder comms if quota increase delayed >2h.
Alisa: Filing an internal mitigation ticket: INFRA-5083 — autoscaler: detect cloud quota errors and mark region degraded. Will include logs and suggested heuristics.
Customer-SRE: Sent message to Acme + updated status page: https://status.redwoodai.com/incidents/5198765432 (note: internal link only)
jen: Logging timeline for postmortem. Noting timestamps and actions for reconstruction.
Mike: Azure SR updated with our telemetry. Also requesting temporary quota reallocation from another subscription owned by our org — asking legal for approval path.
Samir: Leaving this thread to next oncall. Handoff summary: manual routing active; westus2 capacity added; Azure SR open; queued customers prioritized; pausing non-critical batch jobs. I'll be reachable for questions.
SRE-Lead: Good work team. Keep the thread updated with SR changes and when quota increases land. We'll run a full postmortem once stable. :white_check_mark:
oncall-bot: Incident status changed to MITIGATED -> residual impacts, monitoring. Auto-close countdown suspended. Pager cleared for current rotation.
Customer-SRE: Final note: Acme acknowledged receipt and appreciates the rapid mitigation. Continuing to monitor.
